papers.name: Basic Principles of Chemistry and Its Applications in Daily Life

syllabus.topics: Basic Principles of Chemistry: Atoms, molecules, and their electronic structures. Types of Chemical bonding. Basic concept of Hybridization. Energetics of bond formation, Types of intermolecular/intramolecular forces, and molecular association for the formation of materials.

Chemical Reactions: Thermodynamic basis of chemical changes. Enthalpy, entropy, and free energy change during a chemical reaction. Types of Chemical Reactions. The concept of oxidation number, Reducing and oxidizing agents.

Applications of Chemistry in daily life : a) Dyes and pigments: General idea about the chemistry of dyes, Classification of dyes, Origin of the colors in the dyes and pigments, and application in garment and printing industries. b) Polymers: Natural and synthetic polymers, synthesis, properties, and applications. (Examples: polyester, rubber, nylon, bakelite, etc). Introduction to biopolymers. Application of synthetic polymers in surgical treatments and transplantations. c) Food and beverage industry: use of preservatives, food adulteration, flavor enhancers, artificial sweetening agents, and antioxidants. d) Fragrance: Basic principles, types of fragrances, and their applications. e) Cleansing agents: Soaps, detergents, Surfactants, and underlying chemistry of cleansing agents.

Atomic Structure: Wave-particle duality, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, Schrodinger wave equation, Eigenvalues and Eigenfunctions, significance of Ψ and Ψ2 Radial and angular wave functions, Multi-electron system: Concept of Effective Nuclear Charge (Slater's rules).

Atomic properties and their periodic trends: A brief introduction to the modern periodic table (Block wise). Atomic size (Covalent, Ionic and van der Waal's radii; Lanthanide contraction), Electron loss, and electron gain enthalpies. Inert pair effect. Electronegativity (Pauling, Mulliken, Allred Rochow's methods of determination): As a criterion of bond type. Lattice energy and its determination: a) Born-Haber cycle b) Born Lande equation c) Comparison of experimental and theoretical values. Solvation/Hydration energy (Solubility of ionic solids in water). Covalency in ionic compounds (Fajan's rules). Redox reaction, Standard electrode potential and its determination. Electrochemical series and its applications Latimer and Frost diagrams; specific illustrative examples.

Gaseous State: Kinetic theory of gases and ideal gas laws, Maxwell distribution of speed, Equipartition of Energy collisions in a gas: collision number, collision diameter and mean free path, behaviour of real gases: van der Waals equation and its applicability, the critical state: critical constants, law of corresponding states.
Liquid State: Surface tension, capillary action, measurement of surface tension, viscosity of liquids and its measurement, temperature effect on surface tension and viscosity
Solid State: Crystal lattices, space lattice, unit cell, crystal systems, law of rational indices, Miller indices, Bragg's equation, crystal structure of NaCl, graphite and diamond.

Chemical Thermodynamics and its Applications: First law of Thermodynamics, Thermodynamic quantities (w, q, ΔU and ΔH) for isothermal and adiabatic reversible expansion of ideal gases, Kirchoff's relations, Joule effect, Joule-Thomson effect, Joule-Thomson coefficient of real (van der Waals) gases. Second Law of Thermodynamics, Carnot cycle, concept of entropy and its physical significance, entropy changes for an ideal gas, entropy changes at constant pressure and volume, entropy change in spontaneous processes, free energy and maximum work functions, conditions for spontaneous changes and equilibrium, Gibbs-Helmholtz equation, Maxwell relations. Statement of third law of Thermodynamics
Redox titrations: (a) Redox Titrimetric Estimations Based on Iodometry (b) Redox Titrimetric Estimations with standard K2Cr 2O 7 solution
(a) Determination of Surface Tension of liquids. (b) Determination of Viscosity Coefficients of liquids.

Inorganic/Organic Chemistry Laboratory: 1. Preparation of molecular models using wire and beads to study (a) Various hybridization geometries (b) Isomerism 2. Identification of Metal ions by borax bead test 3. Preparation of some simple and double salts. 4. Study of displacement of ions in aqueous solutions (e.g. Cu2+ by Zn) 5. Preparation of m-dinitrobenzene from nitrobenzene 6. Preparation of acetanilide from aniline

Statistical Quality Control Techniques: Statistical treatment of data, Control charts, Performance Evaluation uncertainties in measurement, Validation of analytical methods, Elements of quality Assurance, Principles of Good Laboratory Practices, Good manufacturing Practices in Drugs and Pharmaceutical Industries, Accreditation of QC laboratories, Tools and Mechanisms ICH Guidelines on Drug substances and Products.

Quality Management and Standards: Quality Management System(QMS), Quality management concepts and principles: ISO 9001:2000 QMS, Case studies on ISO 9001: 2000 in chemical industries. ISO 14000 Series of Standards. Total Quality Management (TQM) in Chemical Industry. Six Sigma Approach to Quality: Applying Six Sigma to chemical Industries.
Photosynthesis: Introduction- a key process for life on earth, Light reaction, Dark reaction, Factors affecting photosynthesis, Photorespiration, artificial photosynthesis.

Energy Sources and storage: Introduction to renewable (green) and non-renewable sources of energy. Requirement and consumption of energy in India. Worldwide potential of these sources. Understanding (i) Definition (ii) source (iii) advantages/disadvantages (iv) environmental aspects (v) future scope/sustainability along with specific attributes of each of the following types: Non-Renewable: a) Thermal-Oil, natural gas, and coal Oil - Origin, composition, specification, and characteristics of petroleum products Natural gas - Classification (natural and synthetic gas), Natural gas reserves - India and World Coal: Coal reserves- India and World, Origin, composition, Action of heat on coal, Coal derived chemicals b) Nuclear energy - Radioactivity, Different types of radiation, Nuclear fission, Basic components of Nuclear power reactor. Renewable: a) Solar energy - Importance, storage, applications (solar cooker, solar weather heater, solar greenhouses, solar cell, absorption air conditioning) b) Biomass energy - biomass conversion, biogas generation (types of plants needed, plant wastes, materials), Utilisation of biogas, energy farming (biomass production for energy) c) Fuel Cell d) Li-ion battery
Metals and Metallurgy: Role of metals in our life with special mention of Iron and Copper, Recovery of Iron and copper from its ores, Stainless Steel, corrosion of metals, and its prevention.

Chemical Bonding: i) A comparative account of the Valence Bond (VB) and Molecular Orbital (MO) approach of H2 molecule. Molecular orbital treatment of Homonuclear diatomic molecules of elements of first and second period and Heteronuclear (CO, NO) diatomic molecules. Illustration of HOMO and LUMO. ii) Concept of Hybridization, Bent's Rule, VSEPR theory applied to the compounds of s and p block elements. iii) An introduction to multi-center bonding with illustrative examples of Li-alkyls and diborane. iv) Concept of multiple bonding (p p and p -d) with illustrative examples of BF3, P4O10, (Me3Si)3N and SiF4

Ionic Bonding: A brief introduction to Crystal Packing, Radius Ratio rule, and its exceptions Structures of a few representative crystal types (Rock salt, Zinc blende, Wurtzite, Rutile, Brookite and Anatase).
Metallic Bonding: Theories of bonding in metal: Valence Bond, Free electron, and Band theories.
Weak Interactions: Brief introduction to Hydrogen bonding and other weak interactions: Effects on physical and chemical properties.
Electronic and Field Effect: Electronic (electromeric, inductive, resonance, mesomeric effect, and hyperconjugation) and steric effects on the acidity/basicity of organic molecules.

Stereochemistry: Fischer, Saw-horse and Newman projection formulae. Chirality-optical activity, enantiomerism and diasteroisomerism involving one and two chiral centers. Configuration: D/L, erythrose/threose, R/S nomenclatures; geometrical isomerism - E/Z nomenclatures. Conformations of n-butane.

Hydrocarbons: i. Alkenes: Addition reactions (electrophilic and free radical), hydration, hydroxylation, hydroboration, epoxidation, ozonolysis and polymerization. Addition reactions of conjugated dienes and Diels-Alder reaction. ii. Alkynes: Reduction, electrophilic addition, acidity and metal acetylides

Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic substitution: SN1, SN2 and SNi, Eliminations reactions: E1, E2, and E1cB mechanisms. Elimination versus substitution reactions. Preparation and synthetic applications of Grignard reagents.
Alcohols and Ethers: Preparation and reactions of primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols and ethers.
Active methylene compounds: Preparation and synthetic applications of ethyl acetoacetate and diethyl malonate. (L)
Redox titrations: (a) Redox Titrimetric Estimations Based on Iodometry (b) Redox Titrimetric Estimations with standard K2Cr 2O 7 solution.
(a) Determination of Surface Tension of liquids. (b) Determination of Viscosity Coefficients of liquids.

Metallic Bonding: Theories of bonding in metal: Valence Bond, Free electron, and Band theories.

Electronic and Field Effect: Electronic (electromeric, inductive, resonance, mesomeric effect, and hyperconjugation) and steric effects on the acidity/basicity and reactivity of organic molecules.

Stereochemistry: Fischer, Saw-horse and Newman projection formulae. Chirality-optical activity, enantiomerism and diasteroisomerism involving one and two chiral centers. Configuration: D/L, erythrose/threose, R/S nomenclatures; geometrical isomerism - E/Z nomenclatures. Conformations of n-butane.

Hydrocarbons: i. Alkenes: Addition reactions (electrophilic and free radical), hydration, hydroxylation, hydroboration, epoxidation, ozonolysis and polymerization. Addition reactions of conjugated dienes and Diels–Alder reaction. ii. Alkynes: Reduction, electrophilic addition, acidity and metal acetylides.

Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic substitution: SN1, SN2 and SNi, Eliminations reactions: E1, E2, and E1cB mechanisms. Elimination versus substitution reactions. Preparation and synthetic applications of Grignard reagents.
Alcohols and Ethers: Preparation and reactions of primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols and ethers.
Active methylene compounds: Preparation and synthetic applications of ethyl acetoacetate and diethyl malonate. (L).
Redox titrations: (a) Redox Titrimetric Estimations Based on Iodometry (b) Redox Titrimetric Estimations with standard K2Cr2O7 solution.
(a) Determination of Surface Tension of liquids. (b) Determination of Viscosity Coefficients of liquids.

Inorganic/Organic Chemistry Laboratory: 1. Preparation of molecular models using wire and beads to study (a) Various hybridization geometries (b) Isomerism 2. Identification of Metal ions by borax bead test 3. Preparation of some simple and double salts. 4. Study of displacement of ions in aqueous solutions (e.g. Cu2+ by Zn) 5. Preparation of m-dinitrobenzene from nitrobenzene 6. Preparation of acetanilide from aniline.

Thermoanalytical methods: Thermoanalytical methods: thermogravimetry, factors affecting thermogravimetric curves, derivative thermogravimetry (DTG), thermobalance. Applications of thermogravimetry, differential thermal analysis (DTA), factors affecting DTA curves, instrumentation, and application of DTA. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), theory, instrumentation, applications of DSC, thermometric titrations, and principal classification.

Electrochemical Analysis: Potentiometry fundamentals, reference electrodes (hydrogen, calomel, silver, and silver chloride electrode).Indicator and ion selective electrode, instrumentation and measurement of cell and emf-conductance and conductometric titrations.

Structure Analysis: Diffraction Techniques: Elementary theory (Neutron. Electron and X-ray diffraction), instrumentation, and applications of X-ray methods (emission, absorption, diffraction, and fluorescence methods). Spectroscopic Techniques: Atomic absorption, Spectroscopy, Atomic emission spectrometry, UV-visible molecular absorption spectrometry, Molecular luminescence spectroscopy (fluorescence, phosphorescence, chemiluminescence).

Introduction: Concept and scope of environmental chemistry, Pollution versus contamination, Receptor, Sink, and pathways of a pollutant. Terminology (DO, BOD, COD,TLV) used in environmental analysis and their estimation.

Environmental Segments: Atmosphere- Regions of atmosphere, Carbon Footprint, Greenhouse effect, and Global warming, ozone hole.Hydrosphere- Microorganisms in aquatic chemical reactions, eutrophication versus oligotrophication. Lithosphere- Soil profile, soil properties, organic and inorganic components of soil, micro- andmacro-nutrients.Biosphere.
Natural cycles of the environment:Hydrological cycle, oxygen cycle, nitrogen cycle, phosphate cycle, and sulfur cycle.

Pollution:Sources of air pollution, Auto exhaust emission, and its prevention. Air quality parameters, EL-Nino phenomenon, Water pollution, Acid rains, Waste water treatment: domestic and industrial effluents. Water quality parameters. Recent environmental concerns in the national and global context.

Chemistry of main group elements with special references of the following Flame colorations of alkali and alkaline earth metals. Complexes of alkali and alkaline earth metals (the idea of complexation, examples having inorganic, organic chelating ligands, crowns, electrides, and crypts.). Difference between the first and the other members of the group [Be and other elements, B and other elements]. Metalloids. Allotropes (of C, N, P, O, and S) Hydrides, Halides, Hydroxides, Oxo-acids and their salts, and Oxide With special emphasis on (i) Relevant structures (ii) Acidity and Basicity (iii) Redox behaviour (iv) Stabilities (v) Classification and typical examples, and (vi) General methods of preparation of the aforementioned genres.

Industrial Chemistry: Silicates with examples of practical utilities (Zeolites. Application in Molecular sieves) Glass, Ceramics, Refractories, Cement, Fertilizers(Nitrogenous and Phosphate fertilizers).

Chemistry of Carbonyl compounds: Preparations and reactions - addition and condensation reactions, Cannizzaro, Perkin, Aldol, Benzoin, Haloform, Mannich, and Baylis-Hillman reaction. Important reactions of acids, HVZ reaction, relative reactivity of acid chlorides, acid anhydrides, amides, and esters.
Chemistry of Phosphorous and Sulphur Ylides: Preparation and Reactions. Wittig reaction, Arbuzov rearrangement, Horner- Woodsworth Emons Modification.
Aromaticity: A general concept of aromaticity antiaromaticity and homoaromaticity. Molecular orbital picture of benzene.Benzenoid and non-benzenoid systems, alternant and non- alternant hydrocarbons.

Aromatic Electrophilic Substitution: Mechanism of nitration, halogenation, sulphonation, and Friedel-Crafts (alkylation and acylation) reactions. Effects of substituents on ortho/para ratio, orientation and reactivity.
Preparation and Reactions of Phenols.

Electrochemistry: Arrhenius theory of electrolytic dissociation; Conductance of electrolytes in solution; Ionic conductance, transference number, Determination of transport number by moving boundary method. Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions, ion conductance and ionic mobility, applications of conductance measurements, conductometric titrations.

Chemical Cells and Electromotive Force: Types of Electrodes and electrode reactions, Electrode potential, Standard Electrode potentials, Electrochemical cells, EMF and chemical cell reactions. Free energy, enthalpy and entropy changes of cell reactions; Concentration cells with and without liquid junction, liquid junction potential, salt bridges, applications of EMF measurements.Glass electrode and determination of pH of a solution. Potentiometric titrations: acid-base and redox. Buffer Solutions, Acid-base Indicators.

Phase Equilibria: Thermodynamics of phase transition, Clapeyron-Clausius equation, phase rule, phase diagrams of one-component (water) and two components (phenol-water and Pb-Ag) systems, distribution law, application to cases for dissociation and association, determination of equilibrium constant (KI + I2 = KI3).

Chemical Kinetics: Rate laws for zero, first, and second and Pseudo first-order reactions, steady state approximation, temperature dependence of rates of chemical reactions, Collision theory, qualitative concepts of transition state theory.

Qualitative analysis of simple organic/inorganic compounds: (a) Systematic semimicroanalysis of inorganic salts (mixtures containing 2 cations and 2 anions), (b) Qualitative analysis of simple organic compounds: Preliminary Test, Element detection, Functional group Test, Melting point measurement.

Thermochemistry: Determination of water equivalent of a calorimeter and the enthalpy of neutralization of hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide. Determination of enthalpy of ionization of ethanoic acid. Determination of integral enthalpy of solution of salts.

Introduction to Cosmetics, Soaps, and Detergents: Definition and classification of cosmetics, soaps, and detergents, Historical development and cultural significance, Regulatory framework and quality standards.

Cosmetics: Types of cosmetics (skincare, makeup, haircare, etc.), Cosmetic ingredients and their functions (emollients, emulsifiers, preservatives, etc.), Formulation and manufacturing processes, Packaging and labelling requirements.
Soaps: Saponification process and soap chemistry, Types of soaps (bar, liquid, transparent, etc.), Specialty soaps (medicated, herbal, etc.), Soap additives and fragrances.

Detergents: Types of detergents (household, industrial, personal care, etc.), Surfactants and their role in detergency, Formulation and production processes, Environmental considerations and biodegradability.
Safety, Regulation and Consumer Awareness: Safety considerations in cosmetic and detergent production, Regulatory agencies and compliance requirements, Consumer awareness and product labelling.
Preparation of Soaps, Detergents, and various types of cosmetics.

Purification and drying of solvents: Water and common non-aqueous solvents. Distillation (including fractional distillation and distillation under low pressure). Removal of hazardous impurities from solvents. Drying of non-aqueous solvents.
Synthesis: Preparation of sodium solution in liquid ammonia and its application. Synthesis and Applications of Grignard Reagent.
Click Chemistry: Regioselectivity in Click Chemistry, CuAAC, RuAAC, Bioorthogonal Chemistry, Organocatalyzed Click, Sufex, Thiol-ene Click, and Their Applications.
Reduction using metal hydrides.

Acids and Bases: Brønsted–Lowry, Lux-Flood and Solvent system concepts of acids and bases, leveling effect, Lewis concept of acids and bases and factors affecting their strength, HSAB theory applications: Characteristics of hard-soft acids and bases and borderline cases. Prediction of the feasibility of reactions and stability of compounds, bonding preferences, occurrence of metals as ores in nature, and symbiosis. Super-acids and frustrated acid-base pairs.

Non-aqueous Solvent: Significance of a solvent towards chemical reactions and limitations of water as a solvent. Classification and solvent physical properties for being an effective reaction medium, viz. melting and boiling points, heat of fusion and vaporization, dielectric constant, dipole moment, and viscosity. Liquid NH3 as a non- aqueous solvent, chemical reactions, and alkali metal solutions in liquid NH3. A brief introduction to solvent-free, ionic liquid, and green synthesis.

Transition Metal Chemistry: Characteristics of d-block elements with special reference to 3d transition series (electronic configuration, oxidation state, color, spin- only magnetic moment, complex formation, and catalytic properties.

Coordination compounds: Molecular addition compounds: double salts and coordination compounds. Definition of ligand, denticity. Werner's theory, nomenclature of coordination complexes. Sidgwick's EAN concept and Valence Bond Theory, outer/inner orbital complexes. Geometrical isomerism of coordination compounds with coordination nos. 4 and 6 (Ma6, Ma5b, Ma4b2, Ma3b3, M(aa)3, M(aa)2b2 type). Optical isomerism.

Lanthanides: Separation of Lanthanide elements (Various methods in brief). Comparative study of lanthanide elements with respect to electronic configuration, atomic and ionic radii, oxidation state, lanthanide contraction, and complex formation tendency.

Actinides: Occurrence and preparation of actinide elements. Special reference/method to the enrichment of Uranium. Comparative study of actinide elements with respect to electronic configuration, atomic and ionic radii, oxidation states, compounds, and complex formation tendency.
Nitrogen containing compounds: Preparation and reactions of nitrobenzene and aniline. Preparation and synthetic applications of Diazonium salts.
Heterocyclic Compounds: Nomenclature of heterocyclic compounds, synthesis and reactions of furan, pyrrole, thiophene, pyridine, indole and quinoline.
Polynuclear Hydrocarbons: Chemistry of naphthalene and anthracene.
Colour and Constitution: Synthesis of malachite green, fluorescein, Indigotin.
Alicyclic compounds: Cycloalkanes, general synthesis, Bayer's strain theory. Cyclohexane: chair and boat conformations, conformation of mono substituted and disubstituted cyclohexanes.
Protection and Deprotection of Functional Groups: protection of NH group, OH group, diols, carbonyl groups, carboxyl groups, double bonds and triple bonds.

Carbohydrates: Characteristic reactions of aldoses and ketoses. Glucose-structure (Open and Cyclic), Mutarotation, anomeric effect, iminosugar and sialic acids. Sucrose, starch and cellulose (Structural aspects only), glycosylation reactions.

Thermodynamics of Solutions: Partial molal quantities, chemical potential of a mixture of ideal gases, Gibbs-Duhem equation, chemical potential of real gases and fugacity, activity and activity coefficient, variation of fugacity with temperature and pressure, Lewis-Randall rule, thermodynamic functions of mixing (ΔGmix, ΔSmix, ΔVmix,ΔHmix), ideal solutions and their characteristic properties, Duhem-Margules equation and its applications, Henry and Raoult's laws, thermodynamics of colligative properties, relative lowering of vapour pressure, freezing point depression, elevation of boiling point and osmotic pressure, van't Hoff equation, measurement of osmotic pressure and determination of molecular weight of macromolecules.

Surface and Photochemistry: Langmuir adsorption isotherm, Multi-layer adsorption-BET equation (no derivation) and its application to surface area measurements; Gibbs Adsorption isotherm, surface reactions: kinetics of unimolecular surface reactions, inhibition and activation energy, nature of surface. Enzyme kinetics (Michaelis-Menten equation), Photochemical reactions: quantum efficiency, reasons for low and high quantum efficiency, kinetics of photochemical reactions: decomposition of HI, H2-Br2 reaction, photostationary state: dimerisation of anthracene, Stern-Volmer relation.

Nuclear Chemistry: Radioactivity: general characteristics of radioactive decay kinetics, artificial radioactivity, detection and measurement of radioactivity: GM counter. Nuclear Reactions: Types of nuclear reactions, conservation of linear momentum and mass- energy in nuclear reactions, nuclear reaction cross section. Compound nucleus theory and its experimental verification. Radio chemistry: Probing by isotopes, preparation of radioisotopes, radiochemical principles in use of tracers, some typical applications: chemical, physicochemical and analytical applications, age determination. Radiation Chemistry: Interaction of nuclear radiations with matter- charged particle, neutrons and gamma rays. Radiolysis of water and aqueous solutions, radiation dosimetry.

Introduction to Separation and Instrumental Methods Distillation, Crystallization, Precipitation, Extraction, Chromatography, Introductory ideas of UV-visible spectroscopy, Infrared Spectroscopy, and NMR Spectroscopy.

General Introduction to Analysis, and Stoichiometric Calculations Qualitative and quantitative analysis, primary standard, secondary standard, preparation of standard solutions, molarity, normality, molality, weight/weight percentage, weight/volume percentage, and ppm.

Concepts of Acid-Base Equilibria and Titrations General concepts of acids and bases, strength of conjugate acid/base pair, acid-base equilibria in water, pH calculations for strong acids and strong bases, concepts of acid- base titration, complexometric titration, redox titration, and precipitation titration, indicators.
Complexometric titrations with EDTA: Mg2+, Zn2+ estimation.
Determination of the hardness of water.
Kinetics study of acid catalysed hydrolysis of methyl acetate.
Determination of pH of a given buffer by colour matching method.
Determination of Critical Solution Temperature (CST) of Phenol-Water system.
Effect of impurity on Critical Solution Temperature of Phenol-Water system
